description: A perennial herb 60-100 cm tall with narrow, lance-shaped leaves in two rows on reed-like shoots, and a thick, fibrous, branching, aromatic rhizome. Cone-like flower spikes are rare in cultivated plants.
cultural_significance: Ginger is a kitchen staple and household remedy across India. Shunthi (dried ginger) is called Vishvabheshaja, 'universal medicine', in Ayurvedic tradition.
habitat: Warm, humid climate with rich, well-drained, loamy soil; grown as a rhizome crop in hilly tropical regions.

uses.title: Nausea and indigestion
uses.detail: Fresh ginger with a little salt before meals is traditionally used to stimulate appetite and digestion (Deepana, Pachana).

uses.title: Cough, cold and sore throat
uses.detail: Ginger juice with honey or a decoction with tulsi is a common household remedy; described as Kapha-Vata hara.

uses.title: Joint pain and stiffness
uses.detail: Dried ginger (Shunthi) is traditionally used internally and as a paste for painful joints (Amavata and Sandhivata context).

uses.title: Motion sickness and morning nausea
uses.detail: Clinical studies suggest ginger may ease nausea in some settings; evidence is moderate.

uses.title: Flatulence and colic
uses.detail: Shunthi in warm water or buttermilk is traditionally used for gas and abdominal discomfort.

preparations.name: Ardraka swarasa (fresh juice)
preparations.method: Grate fresh ginger and press out the juice.
preparations.note: Traditionally taken with honey for cough.

preparations.name: Shunthi churna (dried powder)
preparations.method: Dry the rhizome and powder it finely.
preparations.note: Used in many classical formulations including Trikatu.

preparations.name: Ginger tea
preparations.method: Simmer sliced ginger in water for several minutes, strain.
preparations.note: Common household drink; add tulsi or honey.

preparations.name: Shunthi kwatha
preparations.method: Boil dried ginger in water and reduce.
preparations.note: Traditionally used by practitioners in joint and digestive complaints.

precautions: May increase bleeding tendency; use caution with anticoagulants, before surgery, and with diabetes or blood pressure medicines. Excess can cause heartburn or mouth irritation; avoid large medicinal amounts in pregnancy, gallstones and in Pitta aggravation conditions without advice.

cultivation.propagation: Planted from rhizome pieces with 1-2 buds
cultivation.harvest: Harvest 8-9 months after planting (earlier for fresh, tender ginger)

fun_fact: Dried ginger and fresh ginger are treated as different drugs in Ayurveda, with different names and properties.

regions.name: Malabar Coast
regions.note: Kerala is a leading ginger-growing state

regions.name: Southern China
regions.note: Widely cultivated and used in cooking and medicine
